scope (EigenEngine whitepaper)
context window: the fixed-length input a model processes before generating a reply; bounded, so complete re-supply of a growing history is eventually impossible.
lost in the middle: on long inputs a model's recall degrades toward the middle of the window — it attends less reliably to content placed there.
catastrophic forgetting: trained further on new material, a network overwrites what it knew — the connectionist failure named decades ago.

EigenEngine: a persistent, structured memory of one person's body of work AND the research assistant that operates through that memory — one mechanism, not a store with a tool bolted beside it; it is no new model and changes no weights.
conceptric: a graph of concepts arranged in levels of generality, built once when documents enter.
grade: the index of a level of generality — the most specific items at the lowest grade, the broadest summaries at the highest.
atomic proposition: a short record at the lowest grade carrying a single fact drawn from a document (in the Section 7 corpus, one paper is one record).

the fold: building the conceptric — each record grouped with others it shares content with into a cluster, clusters grouped into themes, each grouping decided by content similarity and recorded with the score that produced it.
cluster: a group of records decided by content similarity — the first grouping level of the fold.
summary node: replaces a group, for queries coming from above, by keeping only what its members share.
theme node: the summary node at the top grade of one person's fold.
children / parent: the records under a node are its children; the node is their parent.
base and apex: the bottom of the fold is the base; the small top layer of theme nodes is the apex.
coupling: the number of children two theme nodes share, coupling(A,B)=|children(A) ∩ children(B)| — a set intersection over the apex.
citation-free: a recovered link is citation-free when the two authors share no paper in the corpus, so the thematic overlap is not a by-product of collaboration.
information bottleneck: the code T that forgets as much of the input X as it can while keeping what it must about the target Y, L[p(t|x)] = I(X;T) - β I(T;Y); the principle a theme node approximates.
containment: whether one concept encompasses another — an argument in words, but in a vector space a single componentwise comparison (order embeddings).
identity: whether two records refer to the same person — an essay in words, but in a set representation a membership test.
branching factor b: the average number of children a node has at the grade below; k grades then cover b^k items.
rented intelligence: the large, externally hosted model whose compute is rented by the call; it never sees the corpus and is paid by the sentence.
form conceptric: encodes the manuscript's structural demands — section shapes, figure standards, caption conventions, the house template.
content conceptric: carries the measured results, every number linked by name to its generating script, closed under reproduction.
closure: a check that every concept used in an output has been defined before use.
sealed judge: a separate model call with a fixed, unedited system prompt (the seal), returning a binary pass or flag with the flagged span quoted.
synthetics: the preprint theory of which laws survive when a world is forced through a finite description and which are lost as structured residue — the conceptric is that theory made switch-on-able.
The persistence gap: a language model has no state that survives a session, so it cannot accumulate a structured record of a body of work that grows over time.

The generation gap: keeping no record of what it has asserted, a model cannot check new output against its past for contradiction and falls back on its training, drifting toward the average of everything it has read.

Steering a fixed model closes neither gap: prompting changes what the window holds not whether it survives; fine-tuning cannot hold one growing body of work; RLHF ranks continuations the model already produces; in-context learning moves no weight. Each intervention leaves the store absent.
The store and the assistant are one mechanism: querying the structure is the research work, and the assistant has no knowledge that is not the structure of the store.
The system functions in three moves, all the same descent: the fold at ingestion, recall entering at the apex and descending only as far as it must, and generation as the descent run in reverse.

The one claim, tested: folding documents into this graded structure once makes structural recall logarithmic at zero query-time inference and surfaces cross-author theme links as first-class structural objects recovered by arithmetic over the apex — links that appear in no single document.

The same meaning rides in language or in a vector; a question computationally expensive in one form can become a single arithmetic operation in the other, and a message crosses only as far as the shared code will carry it.

EigenEngine trains no encoder p(t|x): it reaches an approximate code by grouping documents that share content; the bottleneck is invoked to say why the structure has its shape, not as a loss the system minimises.

The fold uses two representations, each for the operation it makes cheap: vectors carry similarity (grouping, nearest theme), sets carry structure (containment, identity, and coupling as a set intersection).

EigenEngine builds its graph backwards from standard ML: a document is assigned to a cluster and a cluster to a theme before it is stored, so the cost of deciding where information belongs is paid once and retrieval traverses structure rather than re-deriving it.

Three precedents make the inversion less strange: distillation carrying a function rather than re-earning it, a deep network as a tower of coarse-grainings (renormalisation), and the brain rebuilding memory from structure with a fast store beside a slow one.

Recall is cheap because the grading is geometric: with branching b a graded hierarchy reaches any of N items in d = ceil(log_b N) grades — depth grows with the logarithm of corpus size, not with the size itself.
The top of a fold is a small layer of theme nodes, not a single root, so a query starting at the apex reaches any document in ceil(log_b(N/A)) steps — about two steps for the Section 7 corpus.

A purely structural query - which themes two authors share - is answered at the apex alone by intersecting the two authors' theme-node sets: no document beneath is read and no model is invoked. The link this establishes is therefore citation-free, its only support the shared apex membership - a fact of the structure rather than a claim asserted in any document.

Generation would reverse the descent: a request enters at the top grade, breaks into sub-questions for the grade below, stops as soon as the structure suffices, and the answers return enriched — predictions down, errors up.
Because the structure is built from one person's own documents, the brief a generative descent assembles already carries that person's conceptual groupings before any prose is composed.

This document is itself an output of the generation move: two conceptrics — a form conceptric of structural demands and a content conceptric of measured results closed under reproduction — were folded by the projector to draft each section.

Each draft entered a panel of four sealed judges — voice, closure, caption-truth, naked-claims — where a flag became the specification for a rewrite, and the projector recurred until the panel returned silence; the author did not edit the prose between iterations.

EigenEngine is a recursive RAG system: it folds retrieved material into a persistent graded hierarchy rather than querying a flat, stateless index on each call, recovering the cross-author link as a first-class structural object at zero query-time inference.

RAPTOR is the closest prior art but rebuilds its tree per corpus, and a paged-memory agent harness persists memory over a flat index — in both, structural relations between documents are never first-class objects and cannot be recovered.

Persistence, metacognition, and most of what is sold as safety are not three problems but one: generative AI runs on constraints — walls we steer it into — when it should run on generators of its own.

A constraint can only forbid; a generator makes. A prompt, a reward, and a fine-tune all act on the model from outside — steering it, bounding it, or reshaping its surface — and none of them installs a source the model runs on itself. The aim is a system driven by generators it owns.

The engine is a ladder of loops, each useless until bootstrapped shut: a loop is primed by hand with a crude first turn and run until it throws off enough of its own substance to carry the next. Closure is a property of one loop on one turn, never of the whole.

The substrate: eight author corpora assembled independently from public records — one target author A and seven collaborators, 1,307 paper-instances (1,202 distinct) — each folded paper → cluster → theme; every number from corpus_experiments.py, every figure from corpus_figures.py.

Result 1 — the fold compresses geometrically: 1,307 papers → 278 clusters → 69 themes, level ratios 4.7 and 4.0, geometric-mean branching b ≈ 4.4; the same slope appears in the engine's full ~5,700-node store over ten grades, evidence the geometric decay is a feature of the fold.

Result 2 — compression strengthens with corpus size: across eight corpora of 29–388 papers a power-law fit gives exponent ≈ 0.23 (R² ≈ 0.56, n=8), so doubling a corpus grows its top layer by only ~17%, an indicative sublinear apex scaling.

Result 3 — structural recall is free and finds what citations cannot: the cross-author set intersection touches the 69 theme nodes, reads 0 of the 1,307 papers, runs 0 model inferences (touched-to-total 0.05); the citation-free fraction ranges 0.61–1.00, mean 0.875 across all eight centres.

The eight corpora and their cross-links: author A plus seven collaborators numbered by corpus size; the strongest thematic coupling is drawn above a normalised similarity of 0.10, distinguishing citation-free links from shared-paper links.
Generation is not solved: the prose is still produced by a general-purpose model whose weights reflect its training corpus, so voice and reasoning are not yet the system's own.

Closing the gap means training an open-weight model on the stored structure — this has not been done; larger corpora, finer grading and a self-hosted generator all require compute beyond what this paper demonstrates.
The sublinear apex exponent (~0.23, R² ≈ 0.56, n=8) is reported as indicative; a larger set of corpora is needed to pin it.
Whether the graded shape follows from one constraint — what survives when a world is forced through a finite description — is a conjecture, not a result; a derivation is left to future work.
Author's note (companion): the prose is 'demented', the last and hardest piece to fix — the engine trying and failing to steer the model it runs on.

narrative: EigenEngine is a persistent structured memory of one person's work and the assistant that operates through it; the fold makes recall cheap; on 1,307 papers it compresses geometrically and recovers citation-free cross-author theme links. Persistence is solved, generation is not.

Two structural gaps limit a language model for a returning knowledge worker: persistence (no state survives a session) and generation (no record of past assertions, so output drifts to the training average). Steering closes neither.
EigenEngine is two things in one mechanism: a persistent conceptric of one person's work and the assistant that queries it; it changes no weights. It makes one claim about the fold and tests it.

The same meaning is expressible as language or as a vector; a question expensive in one form is arithmetic in the other. The information bottleneck says why a theme node keeps only what its documents share. Vectors carry similarity, sets carry structure.

EigenEngine builds its graph in the opposite direction from standard ML: structure is assigned before storage, so the cost of placing information is paid once at ingestion and retrieval is arithmetic. Three precedents make the inversion familiar.
Reading off the cost of the fold: the node count falls geometrically grade by grade, so depth is logarithmic (recall cheap), and a coupling query at the apex is a set intersection that runs no model.

Generation would reverse the descent, assembling a brief the structure has half-composed for a rented frontier model. Persistence is solved and measured; generation — prose in the system's own voice — is not.

One substrate of eight author corpora (1,307 paper-instances), measured three ways: the fold compresses geometrically, compression strengthens with corpus size, and structural recall is free and finds links citations cannot.

The paper is itself an output of the generation move: a form conceptric and a content conceptric were folded by the projector and scored by four sealed judges, recurring until the panel fell silent; the author did not edit the prose.

The eight corpora, assembled independently from public records: author A plus seven collaborators numbered by corpus size, with the strongest thematic couplings and the citation-free cross-link network.

The companion essay, written by the engine: persistence, metacognition and safety are one problem — generative AI runs on constraints when it should run on generators of its own; the engine is a ladder of loops, each bootstrapped shut.
